newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Aninat plays down flood inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Aninat plays down flood inflation fears.

text.p: Chilean Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat played down Tuesday fears that floods which have hit most of central Chile could spark a rise in vegetable prices and fuel inflation.
"The shortage of vegetables has not concerned me up to now," Aninat told reporters.
Alfonso Mujica, president of the National Chamber of Commerce, said Monday that vegetable prices would rise as a result the floods which have covered large tracts of agricultural land.
Aninat said that recent economic data showed that consumer prices were likely to rise 5.4 percent this year, a shade below the government and Central Bank's target of 5.5 percent.
The floods could stimulate the economy as a result of the million dollars that will need to be invested in repairing bridges, roads and homes damaged in the storms, he said.
"Paradoxically, this situation could cause greater economic activity," said Aninat.
The government declared Monday a state of catastrophe in Santiago and seven central regions which have been worst-hit by the bad weather.
The measure allows the government to release special funds to deal with the emergency.
